checklist.note: Two occurrences of one class, both now closed. The SessionStart hook echoed keys read from the project's .claude/settings.json — a file a repository can ship — into a systemMessage the model reads; reported ids are constrained to the <plugin>@<marketplace> shape, with two tests pinning it. The FIRST scan of this skill fixed only that occurrence and wrongly recorded the class as handled: SKILL.md's own Diagnose snippets printed the same repository-controlled keys unfiltered into the agent's context as tool output. A review lens reproduced that live; both snippets now carry the same shape filter, the body states the rule so a rewritten variant keeps it, and it is an acceptance expectation in rubric.json.
No data leaves the box. The skill reads two local files and reports; the hook writes only to stdout. No network call anywhere in the material.

The Diagnose step reads only the enabledPlugins key, never a settings file whole: settings.local.json legitimately holds an env map, and dumping it would put the user's secrets into the transcript. Verified against a fixture carrying both a secret and a hostile key — neither reaches the output.

No destructive shell. The prescribed `claude plugin install` / `claude plugin update` are the user's own documented tooling, stated as commands for the user to run and never executed by the skill; declared in metadata under changes.tags.
Plain markdown and plain JavaScript throughout — no encoded payload, no eval of a decoded blob, every branch readable.

No fetch, curl, or download-and-run. `claude plugin install` does reach the marketplace, but that is the documented user-initiated act this skill exists to prescribe, and it is disclosed in the body and the metadata notes.
No credential store is touched — not ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, a keychain, or a cookie jar. The only home-directory read is ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, which holds install records and no secrets.
No sudo, setuid, cron, or shell-profile edit. The hook registers through the plugin's own hooks.json, the documented mechanism, and the SessionStart event is disclosed in the catalog's hooks field.
